item.title: Digital Agency reports Southern Tohoku workshop on evidence-based policymaking and data use
item.description: AI summary: On 2026-11-27, the Digital Agency reported on its Co-Creation Platform Camp held in Fukushima City, Fukushima Prefecture, on 2026-10-23. The workshop primarily targeted local government staff and brought together 54 participants from 20 local governments, plus one Digital Agency participant. It covered evidence-based policymaking (EBPM), examples from Fukushima City and Utsunomiya City, and hands-on dashboard creation using local finance and population data through Japan Dashboard. item.description: AI summary: The Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications announced a public consultation on 2026-11-20 on a draft ministerial ordinance amending the Fundamental Standards for Establishing Radio Stations (excluding basic broadcasting stations) and related rules. The draft Article 5 would expand permitted communication counterparts for fisheries coast stations to include radio stations aboard non-fishing vessels, while retaining a condition that communications concern the specified persons' fishing activities and be minimal. The package would amend seven ordinances, the Frequency Assignment Plan and related notices, and introduce a new notice establishing technical conditions for autonomous maritime radio equipment. Other listed subjects include ship and aircraft station frequency symbols, distress-alert station equipment testing, ship earth stations and digital selective calling equipment for ship and coast stations. item.title: Draft Cabinet Order aligning mobile subscriber verification and misuse-prevention rules
item.description: AI summary: The Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications announced this draft Cabinet Order consultation on 2026-11-19, with a stated consultation period of 2026-11-20 to 2026-12-21 and a listed deadline of 2026-12-21 23:59 JST. The draft supports Act No. 25 of 2026, promulgated on 2026-05-29, which amends the Act on Identification of Subscribers by Mobile Voice Communications Operators and Prevention of Improper Use of Mobile Voice Communications Services (Act No. 31 of 2005), including extending identity verification at contract conclusion to mobile data communications services. It would amend Cabinet Order No. 171 of 2005 to reflect the renamed Act and expand the offenses specified under Article 8(1)(ii), including specified unauthorized computer access and criminal-proceeds transfer offenses. It would also update references in Cabinet Order No. 146 of 2005 concerning laws covered by whistleblower protection and Cabinet Order No. 180 of 1954 concerning the National Police Agency's organization. The draft specifies commencement on 2027-04-01, alongside the amending Act; it is not presented as a finalized Cabinet Order. item.description: AI summary: The proposed Ministerial Ordinance would relax restrictions on benefits conditional on new mobile-service contracts, allowing installment-based provision of communication-fee discounts and other benefits within a JPY 20,000 ceiling. It would also subject mobile virtual network operators (MVNOs) to the relevant rules when their contract share for regulated services exceeds 4%, regardless of affiliation with a mobile network operator (MNO); the proposed Notice would remove designations of MNO-affiliated MVNOs. The package would amend the Regulations for Enforcement of the Telecommunications Business Act and Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications Notice No. 291 of 2023, under the Telecommunications Business Act (Act No. 86 of 1984).
